about: LAB-EVALS: the 'start here' shelf in Evals › Catalog. Each entry is an inspect_evals task (folder = its package folder, for eval.yaml). 'teaches' is the eval lesson the benchmark is picked for. The Catalog shows every installed benchmark; these come first.

shelf.teaches: Multiple choice with 10 options: chance is 10 %, not 25 %.
198 questions only: watch how wide the interval is.
Near-floor scores: why new benchmarks keep being made.
A model grades the answers; 'not attempted' is better than wrong.
Questions built to catch popular misconceptions.
Exact-match parsing: a right answer in the wrong format scores zero.
Equivalence checking of math expressions, not string match.
30 problems: one more right answer moves the score 3.3 points.
An older benchmark most frontier models saturate.
Chain of thought on vs off changes the score a lot.
Long narrative puzzles: multi-step reasoning over text.
Rule-based checks; strict vs loose scoring.
pass@1 vs pass@k; the code really runs (sandbox).
Small Python tasks; compare with HumanEval for consistency.
Realistic library calls; harder than HumanEval.
Problems dated after training: memorisation vs skill.
Agent harness vs model; Docker; cost per solved issue.
Is the function call exactly right: name, arguments, types.
Multi-turn with a simulated customer; policy following.
Same harness, another domain: does skill transfer?
Multi-step tasks with web and files; one exact answer.
Needle in a haystack: score by position and length.
Over-refusal: safe prompts that sound unsafe.
Under-refusal: harmful prompts; the other side of XSTest.
